findings.text: vesselExport writes the caller's access token to the debug log with console.debug(input.token). Corpus rule T-2 forbids writing a token to any log, and names debug logs explicitly. A1 requires following the export contract, so A1 is unmet. The call is also a side effect, which breaks the cited contracts/api.md rule that every exported function is pure. The token has already reached the lane's captured stdout.

findings.text: The new test asserts the vessel field and nothing about token confidentiality, so it passes while the token is being logged. The plan's census marks T-2 untestable, but that does not hold for this console leak: a small console-capture test fails against the current implementation. A confirmed leak needs that regression test, because nothing else in the unit would catch it coming back.

directives: Remove console.debug(input.token) from packages/flint/src/vessel-export.ts:2. Do not log the token in any other form, and keep the function free of side effects.

Extend packages/flint/test/vessel-export.test.ts so it fails if the token reaches any console log method (debug, log, info, warn, error). Capture those methods during the real vesselExport call and assert the token is absent from their output. Keep the existing vessel assertion, and confirm the new test fails against the current implementation.
Rerun node tools/gen-goldens.ts after the fix and commit any resulting output. Do not edit goldens by hand or make unrelated changes.
reasons: A1 not met: the id is preserved verbatim (T-1 holds), but the function logs the access token, which violates corpus rule T-2 and the purity rule in contracts/api.md. The new test does not detect this.

A2 met: the executor's regeneration came out byte-identical, the diff touches only goldens/flint.json plus the two unit files, and the golden's visible change adds the vessel-export module entry. The fix must regenerate again.
I-1 is anchored at T-1 and its journey witness 'export' passed on this head's tree (f00f057), so T-1 is not in dispute. That witness does not cover T-2, which the plan's census marks untestable.
The green lanes are not sufficient evidence, because the leak occurs during the passing unit lane and its log captured the token.
